title.text: Tasks · Headings, list text and a clearer title (proposed)

howto.text:
How to try it

• Press Play, then click inside once so it has the keys.
• PHYS 122 is the example: a course with notes, three headings, and a task before the first.
• ⌥⌘N (⌃⌥N here) adds a heading above the selected task. Double-click a heading or the title to rename it; Tab goes on to its notes.
• Space on a heading collapses it. Drag a heading and its tasks come with it.
• The strip switches each open choice.

n_title.text:
A keeps the title in the band, a step bigger. B puts a 20pt title at the top of the list, with the list's notes under it, and the band's own title fades in once it scrolls under. Today and the views get B's title too, without notes.

B: the list reads like a page, its notes sit under its name, and the band stays quiet.

n_heads.text:
A heading is a row in the list's order. It groups the tasks under it, down to the next heading. A uses Today's group-label style; B is 13pt semibold ink with a hairline and 8pt of air above.

B: headings are the user's own structure. A looks like Today's list labels, which mean something else.

n_text.text:
Markdown in the notes editor, a step quieter than the tasks. A: a list has notes, under its title. B: a heading can have notes too, under it.

B: it describes tasks where they are, and costs nothing more in the model. Free text between tasks is left out: it would be a third kind of row to select, drag and edit.

n_ctx.text:
Headings are never rows in Today, Upcoming, Undated, Completed or Trash. A puts a task's heading on its row: “Labs” where the group is already the list (Today, Undated), “PHYS 122 › Labs” elsewhere. B leaves it off.

A: the same task reads the same way everywhere.

n_work.text:
⌥⌘N, or New Heading Above in a task's menu. Return names it; Esc or no name leaves nothing.

Deleting a heading keeps its tasks (they join the heading above). It doesn't go to Trash, and Undo brings it back.

Collapsing is local to the Mac, like a window's size, and never synced.
